commit.message:
Set up the design domain: a rulebook, a design-reviewer roster row, its pack, and its verdict on src/public/**

The owner asked for an agent that keeps the desk's page clean, light and modern, serving the
project's intent rather than looking like a live database or a generated app, and judging it for
every project under the operating model. This adds the design domain the way the model sets up a
domain reviewer: the rulebook (governance/domains/design/README.md) with the owner's design rulings,
a refute checklist and periodic audits; the reviewer-class roster row and empty surface; its
context pack; and a [paths."src/public/**"] table requiring its verdict. The agent file,
.claude/agents/design-reviewer.md, is in the Orchestrator's surface and lands in its own commit.

Design rulebook: every standing ruling, a transition rule, two checklist parts, and the conflicts for the owner

The Reviewer failed the first rulebook: it listed only some of the owner's design rulings, and its
checklist enforced the design audit's brief, which is the subject of an open question and goes
against several standing rulings. This lists every standing design ruling on the default branch
(trial-view notes 1 and 2, the design-lab answers and the five agreed screens among them) and puts
them first. Until the owner rules on the redesign direction, a change is judged on part A, which
holds only items traced to a ruling, the frozen spec or a published accessibility standard. Part B,
the audit's brief, applies only to a direction the owner has ruled. Nine places where the brief
and a ruling or the spec disagree are listed for the owner, unresolved. A change that renders
nothing passes with evidence instead of screenshots. Sources are cited by plain path. The pack
may also read the open questions.

Design rulebook, round 2: the owner's newest rulings, later rulings replace earlier ones, fixtures that exist

Round 2 of the review failed the rulebook again. The owner has since ruled the board's scope, the
redesign's five conflicts and text-box size, so those leave the conflicts list and join the
rulings, with the earlier rulings they replace named. Missing standing rulings are added (what
counts as needs-you, usage and context figures, times in America/Chicago, the new design opening
from a tap, new-since markers, batch-2 notes 28 to 31 and 35). The typeface ruling replaces the
font line of the design pick; serving the font from the desk is a spec point, not an owner
conflict. Part A now judges only what a change adds or alters, checks the project fixtures that
exist, quotes the accessibility criteria's own exceptions and the spec's, and applies the board,
tab and typeface rulings. Part B waits for the owner's answer to the redesign direction alone.
The generic-look item becomes an unenforced note, and the no-visible-change path needs evidence
that nothing renders differently.

questions marked as can't-be-undone or settling at their timeout, "With the agents"; project
pages with every standard milestone folded per phase beside the project's own; the Timeline as

tests' fixtures; Personal-Org-Operating-Model on the older pipeline; Members Letter, an example;

Mockup only: nothing is built.

Design rulebook, round 3: "sized like Linear" waits for the next approved mockup; the last missing rulings and conflicts

The owner ruled that the round-3 findings are fixed and the setup goes straight to them. "Sized
like Linear" and Linear's visual formatting are measured against the mockup the owner approves
next and are not enforced until then; until that approval only the 16 px text-box rule is
enforced. The tab, board and typeface rulings stand whatever the redesign-direction answer says,
and a clash would go to the owner. Note 13 is marked as narrowed to colour or icons. Brief 3 is
kept out of part B because its conflict is open. The answering, notification and Work ahead
rulings that touch the page are added, and item 2 covers AC73 to AC76. Two more conflicts are
listed ("Not tied to a milestone", Team's tiles and logs). A board card with one button per option
passes the answering item. One quote now keeps its source's curly apostrophes.

Design rulebook: the owner ruled mockup v2 the direction; sizes measured against it

The owner answered ten questions on 2026-10-20: desk mockup v2, with Home, is the direction for
the whole desk, and the Design reviewer measures "sized like Linear" against it. The hold on the
direction is gone. Part B now judges a change that carries out the direction against mockup v2,
only as far as v2 draws the point, with later rulings applied; sizes are measured against the type
scale v2's README states. The ten answers join the rulings, each naming what it replaces or
narrows (Home first and no Projects tab, full-width tiles, grey Technical, Context and Why labels,
one why line per phase, reviewer verdicts not counted, gate buttons on the card, the portfolio at
Home's foot). Each earlier conflict now says whether v2 takes a side: seven are settled as drawn,
four stay open. The evidence section states that there is no ready way yet to render the fixtures
in a real browser.
